# Habit v1.0.0

The first release of Habit: a calm, Apple-inspired habit tracker that runs in the browser and installs on phones and computers as an app. Everything is stored on your device and it works offline.

## What's new
- **Today** (phone): check off today's habits, see today's progress ring, the current streak and a short insight.
- **Calendar**: a monthly view of every habit (a full grid on desktop, a heatmap with a day-detail view on phones). Past days can be filled in or corrected.
- **Insights**: weekly completion rate, current and longest streaks, monthly consistency and per-habit progress charts.
- **Your habits, your way**: add, edit and delete habits; give each one an icon or any emoji (searchable picker with categories, recently used and paste support) and a preset or fully custom colour.
- **Installable app**: an **Install App** button that opens the browser's own install dialog where one exists (Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet) and step-by-step instructions everywhere else (iPhone and iPad, Safari on macOS, Firefox, in-app browsers).
- **Works offline**: after the first visit the app opens and saves check-ins with no connection.
- **Backups**: export all habits and check-ins to a JSON file and import them on another device or browser.
- **Updates you control**: when a new version is available, Habit says "A new version is ready." and reloads only when you tap **Reload**.

## Improvements
- One consistent button system: pill-shaped text buttons and circular icon buttons, with 44 px touch targets on touch screens.
- Custom colours are contrast-aware, so check marks and icons stay legible on light and dark colours.
- A new minimalist app icon, designed to stay recognisable on the iPhone Home Screen, Android launchers (including round masks), the macOS Dock and the Windows Start menu.
- Desktop and phone layouts share the same data and switch automatically at 820 px.

## Bug fixes
- New habits are scored from the day they were created, so they no longer show as "missed" on earlier days.
- Dates are built from your local calendar, so time zones and daylight-saving changes can't move a check-in to another day.
- The installed app has its own identity when hosted in a GitHub Pages sub-folder, instead of sharing one with every other app on the same domain.
- Unreadable saved data is backed up rather than overwritten.

## Installation
Habit is a web app (PWA). There is no APK or IPA: you install it from the website, and this Releases page records versions and changes.

Open **{{APP_URL}}**, then:

- **Android** (Chrome, Edge or Samsung Internet): go to **Settings → Install App → Install**, or use the browser menu **⋮ → Install app**. Habit opens from your app drawer, full screen.
- **iPhone and iPad**: open the link in **Safari**, tap **Share → Add to Home Screen → Add**. (On iOS 16.4 and later, Chrome and Edge offer the same option in their Share menu.)
- **Windows and macOS**: in Chrome or Edge, click **Install App** in the header or the install icon in the address bar. In Safari 17+ on macOS, choose **File → Add to Dock**.

Already using Habit in Safari on iPhone? Tap **Export backup** in Settings before installing, then **Import backup** in the installed app (see below).

The attached `habit-v1.0.0-web.zip` is the production build for anyone who wants to host Habit themselves on any static HTTPS host. It is not an installer.

## Known limitations
- **No sync between devices.** Each browser keeps its own data; use Export/Import backup to move it.
- **iPhone Home Screen apps keep separate storage** from Safari, so habits tracked in Safari don't appear in the installed app until you import a backup.
- **iOS has no install prompt.** Installing on iPhone and iPad is always done from the Share menu.
- **Firefox on desktop** can't install web apps on most systems; Habit still works there in the browser, including offline.
- Browsers may clear website data after long periods without use; export a backup occasionally.
